notes: This ruleset covers every misconduct category listed in Chapter III (sections 3.1.1–3.7). It does not claim the list is exhaustive; section 3 states additional conduct may be addressed.
Measures are possibilities, not automatic penalties or a mandatory sequence. The Code requires case-specific, proportionate decisions; see section 3, page 9.
The PDF uses printed page numbers in this dataset. For example, printed page 9 corresponds to PDF page 10 if the cover page is counted as PDF page 1.
An empty conditions or exceptions array means none were explicitly specified in that misconduct subsection; it does not imply other Code provisions do not apply.

rules.description: Possession, consumption, distribution, or sharing of alcoholic beverages in violation of applicable laws or regulations. Alcohol use does not itself excuse or mitigate related misconduct and may aggravate serious misconduct.
possible_measures: Seizure of alcoholic beverage, student written statement, warning letter, and community service
Student undertaking and withdrawal of certain privileges
Parent/guardian undertaking
Withholding or deferral of an academic award or other recognition, where applicable
Suspension for a year or expulsion for serious or repeated misconduct of the described kinds while under the influence
conditions: Violation of applicable laws or regulations.
The Code states alcohol use is not by itself an excuse or mitigating factor; where it contributes to or is associated with serious misconduct it may be aggravating.
rules.source_quote: Possession or consumption of alcohol refers to the possession, consumption, distribution or sharing of alcoholic beverages in violation of applicable laws or regulations. Alcohol use shall not, in itself, excuse or mitigate a student’s responsibility for misconduct committed while under the influence of alcohol. Where alcohol use contributes to or is associated with serious misconduct, it may be considered an aggravating circumstance in determining the appropriate disciplinary measure.

rules.description: The University may address under the Code conduct also related to arrest, charge, investigation, or criminal proceedings, in accordance with applicable laws and Code procedures. Criminal process alone is not a finding of misconduct; the University may assess conduct independently and may refer matters to competent authorities.
conditions: Applicable laws and Code procedures apply.
The University independently assesses whether conduct falls within the Code.
exceptions: Arrest, apprehension, investigation, charge, or criminal proceedings do not, in themselves, constitute a finding of misconduct under the Code.
rules.source_quote: Arrest, apprehension, investigation, charge, or criminal proceedings shall not, in themselves, constitute a finding of misconduct under this Code. The University may independently assess the student's conduct where it falls within the scope of this Code, irrespective of whether criminal proceedings have been initiated, are ongoing, or have concluded.
